indication: previously treated metastatic RAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
population_detail: metastatic PDAC after one prior line of chemotherapy; ~92% RAS G12, KRAS G12D included in the G12 stratum
design: randomized open-label phase 3 (RASolute 302), daraxonrasib vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy
median_dor_or_pfs: mOS 13.2 mo (daraxonrasib) vs 6.7 mo (chemo); mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: daraxonrasib arm; chemo 6.7 mo ITT / 6.6 mo G12

safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 43.6% of the daraxonrasib arm versus 57.5% on chemotherapy. The drug-related toxicity is mostly skin and mucosal: grade >=3 rash 14% and stomatitis 12%. TRAE-driven discontinuation was rare at 1.2%, well below the 11.2% seen with chemotherapy.
notes: Pivotal phase 3 behind daraxonrasib's pancreatic development and the FDA breakthrough designation. Sits at second line while this patient is treatment-naive, so it reads as the efficacy anchor for the first-line RASolute 303/305 options rather than a slot he enters now. Per-term grade >=3 rates from ASCO 2026 plenary coverage; NCT06625320.

indication: previously treated advanced RAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
population_detail: 168 PDAC patients dosed <=300 mg after fluoropyrimidine- or gemcitabine-based therapy; efficacy subgroup n=26 RAS G12 at 300 mg in 2L; 68% ECOG 1, 67% liver mets
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 8.5 mo; mOS 13.1 mo; mDoR 8.2 mo (RAS G12, 300 mg, 2L)
safety_summary: Treatment-related AEs were near-universal (96% any grade) but mostly low-grade rash and GI events; grade >=3 TRAEs hit about 30%. Rash dominated at 91% any grade, followed by diarrhea, nausea and stomatitis. Dose modifications were common (~48%) and no patients discontinued for toxicity.
notes: Per-term any-grade AE rates from OncLive/CancerNetwork coverage of the NEJM paper; NCT05379985. Same drug, earlier line than the patient; the response and survival numbers in the RAS G12 subset are the cleanest single-agent read for the KRAS axis.

intervention_dose: 1200 mg PO QD or 600 mg PO BID
population_detail: KRAS G12D PDAC enrolled >=14 weeks before cutoff; prior standard therapy; data cutoff 2 Sep 2024
safety_summary: Well tolerated at 1200 mg/day with no grade 4 or 5 treatment-related events. The common toxicities were low-grade GI: nausea 27%, diarrhea 20%, vomiting 15%, rash 10%, almost all grade 1-2. ALT/AST elevations were rare and mostly grade 1.
notes: ASCO GI 2025 abstract; mature PFS/DoR and 95% CI on ORR not in the abstract. This is the G12D-selective RAS(ON) agent that maps to the patient's exact allele, distinct from pan-RAS daraxonrasib; the front-line phase 3 RASolute 305 builds on it.

intervention_label: INCB161734, oral KRAS G12D ON/OFF-selective inhibitor
indication: advanced/metastatic KRAS G12D pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
population_detail: heavily pretreated KRAS G12D PDAC, all >=2 prior lines, many >=3; monotherapy at RP2D
median_dor_or_pfs: DCR 78%; mPFS and mDoR not reached at ~5 mo follow-up
safety_summary: Manageable as monotherapy and added to gem/nab-paclitaxel or mFOLFIRINOX without cutting chemo dose intensity. Monotherapy GI toxicity ran 50-60% but stayed grade 1-2, with rash and stomatitis notably absent. Grade >=3 neutropenia (~40%) clustered in the chemo-combination cohort; no treatment-related deaths.
notes: ASCO GI 2026 abstract; mPFS/mDoR immature. Second-sponsor G12D-selective agent and the strongest single-agent response rate surfaced in G12D PDAC; motivates the front-line DAWN-303 combination (NCT07522073). First author Wainberg ZA, discussant Ko AH.

exclusion_reason: Program discontinued. The first-in-human phase 1/2 (NCT05737706) was terminated before phase 2 on drug-like-property/formulation grounds, with no efficacy read-out published. Target validity carried forward by zoldonrasib and INCB161734; kept as mechanism history only.

intervention_label: ELI-002 2P, lymph-node-targeted amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine (G12D/G12R + Amph-CpG-7909)
intervention_dose: subcutaneous amphiphile peptides + Amph-CpG-7909 adjuvant, prime/boost
indication: minimal-residual-disease PDAC and colorectal cancer after resection
population_detail: 25 patients (20 PDAC, 5 CRC) ctDNA/biomarker MRD-positive post-resection; HLA-agnostic multivalent design covering G12D and G12R
outcome: mKRAS-specific T-cell response rate; RFS by vaccine-response biomarker
median_dor_or_pfs: median RFS not reached vs 3.02 mo (biomarker-high vs low, HR 0.12)

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: mKRAS T-cell response, 21/25; CD4+ and CD8+ in 71%

outcomes.name: HR_RFS
outcomes.subgroup: T-cell response above 9.17-fold threshold vs below
outcomes.notes: median RFS not reached vs 3.02 mo

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.subgroup: T-cell response above threshold vs below
outcomes.notes: median OS not reached vs 15.98 mo

safety_summary: No grade >=3 treatment-related events and no cytokine release syndrome across 25 patients; treatment-related AEs (48%) were all grade 1-2. The pattern was vaccine-typical: fatigue 24%, injection-site reaction 16%, myalgia 12%. No dose-limiting toxicities, no treatment-related deaths, and no toxicity-driven discontinuations.
notes: Per-term safety from the original Pant 2024 AMPLIFY-201 report (PMID 38195752); the 2025 final-results abstract only says 'no new safety signals.' HLA-agnostic, so the patient's class I genotype does not exclude it, but the MRD/adjuvant setting does not match unresectable metastatic disease. The efficacy split is by on-treatment immune response, not randomization, so it anchors the vaccine mechanism rather than a metastatic efficacy estimate.

exclusion_reason: Superseded by the 2025 final AMPLIFY-201 results (PMID 40790272) from the same cohort with longer follow-up. Retained as the source of the per-term safety table, which the synthesis row cites, but not double-counted as a separate efficacy finding.

intervention_label: pooled mutant-KRAS peptide vaccine + nivolumab + ipilimumab
intervention_dose: pooled synthetic long peptides (6 mKRAS) prime/boost + nivolumab + ipilimumab
population_detail: 12 vaccinated patients; HLA-agnostic pooled peptides covering G12V/G12A/G12R/G12C/G12D/G13D; G12D among the targeted alleles
design: single-arm phase 1 vaccine + dual checkpoint blockade

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: 11/12 with significant increase in average T-cell response across 6 mKRAS antigens

safety_summary: Vaccine-attributed events stayed grade 1-2. The abstract does not break out immune-related toxicity (colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathy) from the nivolumab/ipilimumab backbone, so the per-term irAE profile that matters most for an unselected 79-year-old is not extractable here.

toxicities.notes: abstract reports grade 1-2 only; no per-term rate given

notes: Per-term irAE rates not in the PubMed abstract and PMC full text not retrieved; the nivo/ipi-attributable G3+ immune toxicity is the decision-relevant gap. Shows the vaccine-plus-checkpoint mechanism being tested in immunologically cold, largely MSS PDAC, which is the relevant immunotherapy framing here given MSS/TMB-8.6. Adjuvant setting does not match metastatic disease.

intervention_label: anti-KRAS G12D HLA-C*08:02-restricted TCR-engineered T cells
exclusion_reason: HLA restriction mismatch. The published 72% partial response targeted KRAS G12D presented on HLA-C*08:02; this patient is HLA-C*05:01/C*06:02 (and A*01:01/A*02:01), so the product cannot present his mutant epitope. This is the concrete negative behind case judgment call (b): the C*08:02-restricted TCR-T does not apply, and the NT-112 arm of NCT06218914 carries the same gate.

intervention_dose: 160 mg PO BID, days 1-14 of a 28-day cycle
population_detail: 29 evaluable, ARID1A loss by IHC required; mostly gynecologic (endometrioid endometrial, ovarian clear cell); non-gynecologic tumors under-represented
safety_summary: No treatment-related deaths. Per-term grade >=3 toxicity (the expected ATR-inhibitor cytopenias) was not broken out in the abstract; the class signature from this drug is anemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia.
notes: Per-term cytopenia rates not in the abstract; full text and CT.gov AE tab (NCT03682289) not retrieved, so toxicities[] holds only the death count. The cleanest clinical read on the patient's ARID1A axis: ATR-inhibitor activity concentrates in ARID1A-deficient gynecologic histologies, with the non-gynecologic (PDAC-relevant) signal weaker, and entry gated on BAF250a IHC loss rather than the frameshift call alone.

exclusion_reason: ARID1A not in the selected-biomarker list. TRESR enriched for ~18 DDR loss-of-function genes (ATM, BRCA1/2, CDK12, SETD2 and others) but not ARID1A, and reported no ARID1A cohort, so it gives ATR-class precedent without testing the patient's actual synthetic-lethal vulnerability. Class-toxicity reference: grade 3 anemia ~26%, the dose-limiting ATR-inhibitor effect.

First-in-human dose-finding without an ARID1A-selected cohort or PDAC efficacy signal; the only response was a single unconfirmed PR in BRCA-wildtype ovarian cancer. Mechanism support for the ATR axis only. Class toxicity is marked: grade >=3 anemia 36%, any-grade anemia 71%, with 11 DLTs (mostly anemia). The ARID1A loss-of-function arm of DDRiver 320 (NCT05396833) is the construct that would actually test this patient's axis.

Negative cross-tumor read plus drug withdrawal. NRG-GY014 tested the ARID1A-EZH2 synthetic-lethal hypothesis in ARID1A-context endometrioid endometrial and ovarian clear cell cancer and closed early for futility (endometrial cohort stopped after stage 1, accrual closed Jun 2022); specific ORR not retrievable from the paywalled paper. Tazemetostat was subsequently withdrawn from all trials/markets on an unfavorable benefit-risk read, so the EZH2 route into the patient's ARID1A axis lost both its supporting efficacy signal and its lead agent.

intervention_label: GFH375 / VS-7375, oral KRAS G12D(ON/OFF)-selective inhibitor
indication: previously treated advanced KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
population_detail: 66 KRAS G12D PDAC treated at 600 mg QD, 59 evaluable with >=1 post-baseline assessment; 45/66 (68%) had >=2 prior lines; median exposure 117 days
design: phase 1/2 open-label monotherapy dose-expansion, single-arm (GFH375X1101, China)
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 5.52 mo (90% CI 4.27-7.20); 3-mo PFS ~83%; DoR not reported

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade >=3 TRAE (20 patients); one grade 4 neutropenia

safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 30% (one grade 4 neutropenia), with the burden split between GI toxicity and myelosuppression. Diarrhea (56% any grade), decreased neutrophils (49%), nausea and vomiting (47% each), and anemia (42%) were the commonest events; grade >=3 rates stayed low apart from neutropenia (8%) and anemia (8%). No dose-limiting toxicities at the 600 mg dose.
notes: Per-term AE rates from the Verastem/GenFleet ESMO 2025 release (data cutoff 27 Aug 2025; NCT06500676). Same drug as the patient's newly-added VS-7375 1L+cetuximab (NCT07644559) and GFH375 phase 3 (NCT07262567) options; the evidence sits one line beyond the treatment-naive patient. G12D-selective ON/OFF inhibitor mapping to his exact allele.

intervention_dose: 800 mg or 1200 mg IV every 2 weeks
indication: advanced KRAS G12D-mutant solid tumors (NSCLC and PDAC subsets)
population_detail: 84 KRAS G12D solid tumors after chemo/immuno/targeted therapy; PDAC and NSCLC subsets reported; MTD not reached
median_dor_or_pfs: PDAC mPFS 4.4 mo (95% CI 2.6-7.2) at 1200 mg; PDAC mOS not reached
safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 23.8%, with a metabolic rather than GI signature: hypertriglyceridemia, neutropenia and hypercholesterolemia were the characteristic events. One treatment-related death and one TRAE-driven discontinuation; MTD not reached.
notes: Per-term grade >=3 rates not fully broken out in the ESMO daily-reporter coverage; only the top-3 characteristic terms and the 23.8% union rate are given. Monotherapy read for HRS-4642, one line beyond the treatment-naive patient; the front-line combination is the enrollable HRS-4642 option (NCT07232875).

intervention_dose: HRS-4642 500 mg IV day 1 + 1200 mg IV day 8, every 3 weeks (RP2D) with gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel
indication: advanced KRAS G12D-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, front-line
population_detail: 31 treated (30 treatment-naive, 1 previously treated); phase 2 efficacy analysis in 30 treatment-naive patients
design: phase 1b/2 single-arm, HRS-4642 added to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel (NCT06520488)
median_dor_or_pfs: median follow-up 12.3 mo; mPFS/mOS not yet reported in abstract

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade >=3 TRAE, mostly hematologic per AG backbone

safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 90.3%, driven by the gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel hematologic toxicity rather than a new HRS-4642 signal. No dose-limiting toxicities in phase 1b; the safety profile tracked the chemotherapy backbone.

toxicities.notes: primarily hematologic, consistent with AG chemotherapy

notes: Peer-reviewed phase 1b/2 (data cutoff 5 Dec 2025); no PubMed record yet, cited by DOI. This is the front-line combination read behind the newly-added phase 3 HRS-4642 + gem/nab-paclitaxel (NCT07232875), which matches the patient on allele, tumor type and 1L. Per-term grade >=3 breakdown not in the abstract; toxicities[] holds only the union rate.
